It's not so much food at the funeral, but more-so food before and/or after. It's usually set up buffet style where people can go grab what they want, as much as they want, go back for more and repeat. The Wake (after the funeral) is usually where most of the food is.

From previous deaths in my family, we congregate almost immediately after the person has died. Someone's usually got a meat and cheese platter handy, or can get one whipped up real quick at a supermarket. Alcohol is always present in my family. Over the course of the few days preceding the funeral, people show up to express their condolences and provide an offering of food (casseroles, pre-made sandwiches, meat and cheese platters). The funeral is then attended and the wake is immediately after. The wake can be food as mentioned above, but can go so far as to be fully catered (I've never been to a fully catered one). The entire process is, of course, filled with potato chips, dip, and sugary snacks (cookies, ice cream, chocolates, cakes, and soda).

Social eating is more a comfort thing. Many fat people are comforted by eating their feelings instead of actually dealing with them.
